title: Salt and Choir
premise: Zephyrine Villalobos, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has survived seven years in Vellamare by hiding his magic beneath lawful craft. When a century-old prophecy names tonight's date as the night the covenant between the living city and the drowned realm of Salt breaks, Zephyrine discovers he is not merely foretold—he is the instrument of it. Hunted by the Ministry of Unmaking and courted by the dead who want their covenant restored at any cost, he must choose between the woman he loves, who enforces the anti-magic law, and the survival of both realms. In the end, Zephyrine reforges the covenant with his own carved bones as its keystone, paying the price of his hearing—silencing the dead forever—and choosing love freely given rather than duty imposed.
about_author: Hazel Okonkwo is the pen name of a former cathedral restorer who spent a decade repairing centuries-old bone crypts before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about craftspeople, covenants, and the quiet violence of laws that outlaw what people cannot help being.

chapters.title: The Date Written in Water
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Selling charms in Vellamare's night market, Zephyrine hears a drowned voice recite his own name from a prophecy dated one hundred years past—tonight. He dismisses it until the Ministry raids the market hunting 'the Carver.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the fragile peace of hidden identity cracking.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleeing through the bone-carvers' quarter, he consults the ossuary archive and finds the full prophecy: a broken covenant, a reforge, and a price written in a script only the dead can read. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance—the past claiming him whether he consents or not.

chapters.title: The Warden of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Isolde Ferreol's POV. The Ministry warden who once loved Zephyrine is ordered to arrest him. She burns her copy of the prophecy instead and goes looking for him off the record. Emotional beat: love against duty begins its war inside her.

chapters.title: Low Tide at the Drowned Gate
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Following the prophecy's first instruction, he reaches the sunken gate where the covenant was sealed and meets the Choir—a parliament of the dead who demand he reforge what his ancestor broke. They show him the price: his hearing, willingly surrendered. Emotional beat: awe curdling into coercion.

chapters.title: A Law Made of Ash
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde uncovers that the Ministry's founder wrote the anti-magic law using a forged prophecy—to starve the covenant and hoard its power for the state. Her certainty in the law collapses. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution she gave her life to.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reunited with Isolde, Zephyrine learns the Ministry plans to kill him at the next tide and harvest his gift. The dead offer protection—for a promise he isn't sure he can keep. Emotional beat: tenderness under threat; two outlaws building trust from wreckage.

chapters.title: Choir of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The couple descends into Salt itself, where the dead reveal the covenant's true terms: it was never meant to be enforced by law, but renewed by choice each generation. The Ministry's theft has starved both realms. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything—duty was always a distortion of love.

chapters.title: The Tide That Takes Names
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The Ministry, led by Isolde's mentor Archivist Corvane, breaches Salt with an engine built to devour the covenant entirely. Isolde turns her badge, her rank, and her body against them. Emotional beat: the cost of defection paid in full, without hesitation.

chapters.title: Reforge
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the breaking heart of the covenant, Zephyrine carves his own bones into the keystone as the Choir demands—but refuses their coercion, offering the sacrifice as a free gift instead, which alone can seal it. Corvane falls into the tide his engine raised. Emotional beat: climax—love chosen, not compelled, becomes the only magic that holds.

chapters.title: Silence, and the Sound After
chapters.summary: Shared final chapter. The covenant holds; the dead go quiet in Zephyrine's ears forever, and magic returns lawfully to Vellamare under a new, chosen accord. Deaf to ghosts but not to Isolde, Zephyrine opens a small shop that sells no charms at all. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—survival's price paid, identity remade, love remaining.
